mainTopic: Mistakes in קריאת שמע, workers' obligations in קריאת שמע, תפילה and ברכות, and the exemption of a חתן and one busy with a מצוה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a דרשה: just as streams raise a person from טומאה to טהרה, tents of Torah raise a person from guilt to merit. Next comes a story about רבי אלעזר, who left his own wedding preparations to hear a ברייתא before רבי יוחנן. The ברייתא says where to go back to if you lose your place in קריאת שמע, and רבי יוחנן adds a limit to it. A new משנה then teaches that workers may say קריאת שמע at the top of a tree or wall but not the עמידה. It also teaches that a חתן is exempt from קריאת שמע, though רבן גמליאל chose to say it anyway. The גמרא asks whether reciting up a tree means no כוונה is needed. It answers that workers stop working for the first paragraph and may keep working during the second. It then shows that hired workers may shorten their davening and ברכת המזון, depending on whether they are paid a wage or only a meal. Finally, the גמרא learns from the words ״בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ בְּבֵיתֶךָ וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ״ that someone busy with a מצוה, and a חתן, is exempt from קריאת שמע.

steps.title: Tents of Torah lift a person like streams do
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק places 'tents' next to 'streams' to teach that Torah study raises a person from guilt to merit, just as streams raise a person from טומאה to טהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are tents placed next to streams? Because the פסוק says: 'Like streams stretched out, like gardens by the river, like tents planted...' This teaches you: just as streams lift a person from טומאה to טהרה, so too tents of Torah lift a person from the side of guilt to the side of merit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a דרשה that began on the previous amud. It explains why the פסוק mentions tents right next to streams.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, 'tents' stands for the tents of Torah study, the places where people learn. Just as someone who is טמא dips in flowing water and comes out טהור, someone who learns Torah is moved from the guilty side of the scale to the side of merit.

keyTerms.meaning: Tents; here, the tents where Torah is learned
Streams or rivers of flowing water

phrases.english: Tents next to streams,
as it is written: 'Like streams stretched out,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:6

phrases.english: like gardens by the river,
like tents planted, etc.'
to tell you: just as streams
raise a person from impurity to purity,
so too tents raise a person
from the scale of guilt to the scale of merit.

steps.whatToRemember: Learning Torah is like dipping in a stream: it lifts a person from guilt to merit.
steps.triggerLanguage: לומר לך: מה נחלים מעלין את האדם מטומאה לטהרה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the דרשה about tents and streams that began in the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tents of Torah raise a person from guilt to merit, just as streams raise a person from טומאה to טהרה.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: reading קריאת שמע out of order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: someone who reads קריאת שמע out of order has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: one who reads קריאת שמע out of order has not fulfilled his obligation, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that קריאת שמע has to be said in its proper order. The 'and so on' points to the rest of the משנה: someone who made a mistake goes back to the place where he went wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not fulfill his obligation

phrases.english: 'One who reads out of order
did not fulfill his obligation, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the aggadic teaching to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading קריאת שמע out of order does not fulfill the obligation.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר goes to the study hall during his wedding preparations
steps.stepSummary: While רבי אמי and רבי אסי tie a wedding canopy for רבי אלעזר, he goes to the בית מדרש and finds a תנא teaching before רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי were tying a wedding canopy for רבי אלעזר. He said to them: in the meantime, I'll go hear something new in the study hall, then come back and tell you. He went and found the תנא who was reciting before רבי יוחנן:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that leads into a teaching about mistakes in קריאת שמע. It ends by setting up the next step, the ברייתא that רבי אלעזר heard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even on his wedding day, רבי אלעזר used the spare time to learn something new and share it with his friends. The story is how the גמרא brings in the ברייתא about losing your place in קריאת שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who memorized and recited teachings in the study hall

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi
were tying a wedding canopy
for Rabbi Elazar.
He said to them: In the meantime,
I will go and hear something in the study hall,
and I will come back and tell it to you.
He went and found the reciter
who was reciting before Rabbi Yochanan:

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי אמי ורבי אסי הוו קא קטרין ליה גננא לרבי אלעזר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a story to introduce a ברייתא related to the משנה about mistakes in קריאת שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story that introduces the ברייתא heard before רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Where to go back to after losing your place in קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that someone who made a mistake in קריאת שמע and doesn't know where goes back to the earliest place he might have been.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone read קריאת שמע, made a mistake, and doesn't know where he made it. If he is in the middle of a paragraph, he goes back to the beginning of that paragraph. If he is between paragraphs, he goes back to the first break between paragraphs. If he is unsure which 'writing' verse he was up to, he goes back to the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the ברייתא רבי אלעזר heard. It gives the rules for where to go back to when you lose your place in קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea in every case is to go back to the earliest spot you might have been, so nothing is skipped. The 'writing' case is a classic mix-up: the פסוק 'וכתבתם על מזוזות ביתך' appears in both the first and second paragraphs, so you go back to the one in the first paragraph.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Writing'; the פסוק 'וכתבתם' (and you shall write them)

phrases.english: One who read and made a mistake
and does not know where he made the mistake:
in the middle of a paragraph, he goes back to the beginning.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין פֶּרֶק לְפֶרֶק — יַחְזוֹר לְפֶרֶק רִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.english: Between one paragraph and another, he goes back to the first paragraph break.
Between one 'writing' and the other 'writing',
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק 'וכתבתם על מזוזות ביתך', which shows up in both the first and second paragraphs (דברים 6:9, 11:20).

phrases.english: he goes back to the first 'writing'.

steps.whatToRemember: If you lose your place in קריאת שמע, go back to the earliest spot you might have been: the start of the paragraph, the first break, or the first 'וכתבתם'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule for anyone who loses focus while saying קריאת שמע.
steps.triggerLanguage: קרא וטעה ואינו יודע להיכן טעה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the teaching רבי אלעזר heard in the study hall, introduced by the story in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When unsure where you made a mistake, go back to the earliest possible point: the start of the paragraph, the first paragraph break, or the first 'וכתבתם'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits the rule about going back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the rule of going back to the earliest place applies only if the person has not yet reached 'למען ירבו ימיכם'. If he has, we assume his habit carried him through the second paragraph.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This rule only applies if he hasn't started 'In order to lengthen your days'. But if he has started it, he just followed his usual routine and kept going.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן, hearing the תנא recite the ברייתא, adds a limit to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a person unsure of his place goes back to the earliest point he might have been. רבי יוחנן says that if he is already saying 'למען ירבו ימיכם', the line that comes right after 'וכתבתם' in the second paragraph, we trust that habit brought him there correctly. In that case he does not need to go back.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in a case where... (a phrase that limits a rule)
he followed his habit or routine
'In order to lengthen your days', a line in the second paragraph of שמע

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that, in prayer, the גמרא trusts a person's well-practiced habit when he is unsure what he said.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
They only taught this
where he did not begin 'In order to lengthen your days',
phrases.notes: דברים 11:21

phrases.english: but if he began 'In order to lengthen your days',
he followed his routine and kept going.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא quoted in step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once he has begun 'למען ירבו ימיכם', he assumes he finished the second paragraph correctly and does not go back.

steps.title: The Rabbis treasure רבי יוחנן's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר tells רבי אמי and רבי אסי what he heard, and they say it alone was worth the trip.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came and told them. They said to him: If we had come only to hear this, it would have been enough for us.
steps.whatsHappening: The story from step 3 ends. רבי אלעזר brings the teaching back, and his colleagues praise it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי and רבי אסי had stayed behind, busy with the חופה. They say this one teaching alone was worth everything. This shows how much they valued a precise detail in the laws of קריאת שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: it would have been enough for us

steps.whatToRemember: Someone who loses his place goes back to the earliest point he might have been. But once he has reached 'למען ירבו ימיכם', he trusts that he finished correctly.

phrases.english: He came and told them.
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר went back to רבי אמי and רבי אסי, who were tying the חופה.

phrases.english: They said to him:
If we had come
only to hear this thing,
it would have been enough for us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִלּוּ לֹא בָּאנוּ אֶלָּא לִשְׁמוֹעַ דָּבָר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story that frames רבי יוחנן's teaching
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's limit on the rule was seen as a very valuable teaching.

steps.title: Workers may recite שמע while up high
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: workers may say קריאת שמע at the top of a tree or a wall, but they may not say the עמידה there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Workers may recite קריאת שמע at the top of a tree or at the top of a row of stones. They are not allowed to do this for the עמידה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It compares how much focus קריאת שמע needs with how much the עמידה needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קריאת שמע can be said even while standing in an unsteady, high place during work. The עמידה is different. It needs full focus of the heart, so a worker must come down to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: a row or layer of stones in a wall being built

steps.confusionAlert: In the משנה, 'תפלה' means specifically the עמידה, not prayer in general.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The workers
recite at the top of the tree
and at the top of the row of stones.
which they are not permitted
to do for the תפלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Workers may say קריאת שמע while up high at work, but not the עמידה.

steps.title: A groom is exempt from שמע
steps.stepSummary: A חתן is exempt from קריאת שמע from the first night until מוצאי שבת, as long as he has not yet consummated the marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: A groom is exempt from קריאת שמע on the first night and until Saturday night, if he has not yet done the act.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another rule about focus: a חתן is exempt from קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new חתן is too worried and distracted to focus. So he is freed from קריאת שמע until the marriage is consummated, or until מוצאי שבת at the latest.

phrases.english: A groom is exempt from קריאת שמע
on the first night
and until Saturday night,
if he has not done the act.
phrases.notes: He means: if he has not yet consummated the marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next rule in the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חתן is exempt from קריאת שמע until he consummates the marriage, or until מוצאי שבת.

steps.title: Students question רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל said קריאת שמע on his wedding night. His students ask: didn't you teach us that a חתן is exempt?
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story with רבן גמליאל: he married a woman and recited שמע on the first night. His students said to him: Didn't you teach us, our teacher, that a groom is exempt from קריאת שמע?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story. The students point out that their teacher's action seems to go against his own teaching. This sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule just taught is that a חתן is exempt. So the students want to know why רבן גמליאל said קריאת שמע anyway.

phrases.english: And there was a story with Rabban Gamliel
who married a woman
and recited on the first night.
His students said to him:
Didn't you teach us, our teacher,
that a groom is exempt from קריאת שמע?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the rule of step 8 against רבן גמליאל's own behavior
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל saying קריאת שמע on his wedding night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He taught that a חתן is exempt, yet he said קריאת שמע himself.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל will not give up Heaven's kingship
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל answers that he will not give up accepting מלכות שמים, even for one moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I will not listen to you and remove from myself the Kingdom of Heaven, even for one moment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל explains why he chose to recite even though he was exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not deny the exemption. He chooses to recite anyway, because קריאת שמע is accepting the yoke of מלכות שמים, and he refuses to go without it even briefly.

keyTerms.meaning: the Kingdom of Heaven, accepting God as King

steps.whatToRemember: A חתן is exempt from קריאת שמע because of his worry. Even so, רבן גמליאל chose to say it, because he would not give up מלכות שמים even for a moment.
steps.confusionAlert: רבן גמליאל is not saying the rule is wrong. The exemption still stands; he simply chose to go beyond it himself.

phrases.english: He said to them:
I will not listen to you
to remove from myself the Kingdom of Heaven
even for one moment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question
steps.terutzResolutionType: Personal choice to go beyond the exemption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a חתן is exempt, רבן גמליאל should not have said קריאת שמע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption stands, but he chose not to give up מלכות שמים even for a moment.

steps.title: A ברייתא adds details about workers on trees
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that workers may say קריאת שמע on a tree or wall. They may daven on an olive or fig tree, but must climb down from other trees. A בעל הבית must always climb down to daven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Workers may say קריאת שמע at the top of a tree or a wall. They may daven at the top of an olive tree or a fig tree. For all other trees, they climb down and daven. A homeowner always climbs down to daven, because his mind is not settled up there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of our משנה by quoting a ברייתא that adds more detail about workers saying קריאת שמע and davening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה (step 7) said workers may not say the עמידה on a tree. The ברייתא adds an exception: on an olive or fig tree they may daven, but on other trees they must come down. A בעל הבית gets no exception at all, because his mind would not be settled enough to daven up there.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this introduces a ברייתא
Workers or craftsmen hired to do a job
A row of stones in a wall being built
The homeowner, the owner of the field or building
His mind is settled and calm enough to focus

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two activities. Saying קריאת שמע ('קורין') is allowed on any tree. Davening the עמידה ('מתפללין') is only allowed on an olive or fig tree.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
Workers may recite [שמע] at the top of the tree
and at the top of the row of stones.
And they may daven at the top of an olive tree or a fig tree.
But for all the other trees,
they climb down and daven.

phrases.aramaic: וּבַעַל הַבַּיִת, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ
phrases.english: And the homeowner, in either case,
climbs down and davens,
because his mind is not settled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה from step 7 by bringing a ברייתא that adds detail to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Workers may say קריאת שמע on any tree or wall. They may daven only on an olive or fig tree. A בעל הבית must always climb down to daven.

steps.title: Does קריאת שמע need focus or not?
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בריה דבת שמואל asks רבא: our משנה lets workers recite on a tree, which suggests no כוונה is needed. But a ברייתא learns from a פסוק that קריאת שמע does need כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי, the son of שמואל's daughter, asked רבא: Our משנה says workers may recite on a tree or wall, so it seems no focus is needed. But a ברייתא says: whoever says שמע must focus his heart. The פסוק says 'שמע ישראל', and later it says 'הסכת ושמע ישראל', pay attention and hear. Just as there it means paying attention, here too it means paying attention.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי points out that two sources seem to clash. One suggests you can say קריאת שמע without focus, and the other says you must focus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being up on a tree or wall, a worker is busy and nervous, so if the משנה allows קריאת שמע there, it seems כוונה isn't needed. But the ברייתא links the word 'שמע' in our פסוק to the same word in a later פסוק that says 'הסכת', pay attention. So קריאת שמע does require כוונה, and the two sources contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: He pointed out a contradiction between two sources
So we see; this draws a conclusion
Focus or intention of the heart
And they set it against another source; this introduces the clashing source

phrases.english: רב מרי pointed out a contradiction
the son of שמואל's daughter, to רבא:
We learned: Workers may recite
phrases.notes: This is the משנה from step 7.

phrases.english: at the top of the tree and the top of the row of stones.
So we see it does not need focus.
But this clashes with another source: One who recites שמע
must focus his heart,
as it says: 'Hear, Israel,'
phrases.notes: דברים 6:4

phrases.english: and later on it says:
'Pay attention and hear, Israel.'
phrases.notes: דברים 27:9

phrases.english: Just as there it is with 'paying attention,'
so too here it is with 'paying attention.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב מָרִי בְּרַהּ דְּבַת שְׁמוּאֵל לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the workers' rule by drawing an inference from it and setting it against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה allowing workers to say קריאת שמע on a tree or wall.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If workers may recite in such a distracting place, then כוונה is not needed. But a ברייתא derives from 'הסכת' that קריאת שמע does require כוונה.

steps.title: רב ששת: the workers stop working to recite
steps.stepSummary: רבא is silent. He asks רב מרי if he has heard an answer. רב מרי quotes רב ששת: the workers may recite on the tree only if they stop working while they say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא was silent. He asked רב מרי: Have you heard anything about this? רב מרי answered: This is what רב ששת said: The rule applies only when they stop their work and recite.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא has no answer, so רב מרי gives the answer he heard from רב ששת. The workers really do focus, because they stop working while saying קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's answer removes the contradiction. The משנה never meant that workers may recite without כוונה. They stay up on the tree, but they pause their work, so they can still focus as the ברייתא requires.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent; he had no answer
And this applies only when; this sets a condition on the rule

phrases.english: He was silent.
phrases.notes: It's רבא who goes quiet, because he has no answer.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִידֵּי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ בְּהָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Have you heard anything about this?
phrases.notes: Now רבא is asking רב מרי if he knows an answer.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת —
phrases.english: He answered him: This is what רב ששת said:
It applies only when they stop their work and recite.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת — וְהוּא שֶׁבְּטֵלִין מִמְּלַאכְתָּן וְקוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה is limited to workers who pause their work.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Workers may say קריאת שמע on the tree while still working, so no כוונה is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: They stay on the tree but stop working while reciting, so they do have כוונה.

steps.title: בית הלל say workers keep working while reciting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת from a ברייתא where בית הלל say workers keep doing their work while they recite קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: בית הלל say that workers keep busy with their work and recite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב ששת's answer with a ברייתא that seems to say the exact opposite. The answer to this challenge comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said the workers must stop working. But this ברייתא quotes בית הלל saying workers recite while they keep working. That seems to bring back the original problem of reciting without full focus.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? This opens a challenge
They keep busy with their work

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: בית הלל say
they keep doing their work and recite!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's answer from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the workers must stop working to recite.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes בית הלל saying workers keep working while they recite, which directly contradicts the requirement to stop.

steps.title: First paragraph versus second paragraph
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says both sources are right. Workers must stop working for the first paragraph of קריאת שמע, but they may keep working during the second paragraph.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a contradiction: one source is talking about the first paragraph, and the other is talking about the second paragraph.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 14 by saying each source is talking about a different part of קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said workers must stop working, but the ברייתא of בית הלל said they keep working. The answer is that the first paragraph needs extra כוונה, so they must stop for it. For the second paragraph they may keep working.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.whatToRemember: Workers must stop working for the first paragraph of קריאת שמע, which needs כוונה. They may keep working during the second paragraph.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about the first paragraph,
phrases.notes: "This one" is רב ששת's rule that the workers must stop working.

phrases.english: that one is about the second paragraph.
phrases.notes: "That one" is the ברייתא of בית הלל, where workers keep doing their work.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּפֶרֶק רִאשׁוֹן, הָא בְּפֶרֶק שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different paragraph
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת and the בית הלל ברייתא seemed to argue about workers during all of קריאת שמע
steps.terutzMaskana: Workers stop for the first paragraph and keep working during the second paragraph

steps.title: What workers say while working for a homeowner
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that workers say קריאת שמע with its ברכות, say ברכות on their bread, and daven the full שמונה עשרה. They do not serve as שליח ציבור, and the כהנים among them do not say ברכת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Workers doing work for a homeowner recite קריאת שמע with the blessings before and after it. They eat their bread and say the blessings before and after it. They daven the full שמונה עשרה. But they do not lead the davening, and they do not lift their hands for ברכת כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the obligations of workers. It sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists everything workers still must say, including the full שמונה עשרה. It also lists two things they skip, leading the davening and ברכת כהנים, since those are extras that take more time.

keyTerms.meaning: Going down before the ark, meaning leading the davening as שליח ציבור
Lifting their hands, meaning saying ברכת כהנים

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Workers who were doing work
for a homeowner
recite קריאת שמע
and say the blessings before it and after it.
And they eat their bread
and say the blessings before it and after it,
and they daven the prayer of eighteen blessings.
But they do not go down before the ark,
phrases.notes: This means they do not lead the davening as the חזן.

phrases.english: and they do not lift their hands.
phrases.notes: The כהנים among the workers do not say ברכת כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַפּוֹעֲלִים שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹשִׂין מְלָאכָה אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the full list of workers' obligations
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Workers say קריאת שמע and its ברכות, say ברכות on their bread, and daven the full שמונה עשרה. They do not lead the davening or say ברכת כהנים.

steps.title: Another source says workers say a shortened שמונה עשרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא that says workers say only a shortened version of שמונה עשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught that workers say a shortened version of שמונה עשרה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from Step 16 with another ברייתא that says the opposite about שמונה עשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said workers daven the full שמונה עשרה. This other ברייתא says they daven only a short summary of it. The two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)? This introduces a contradicting source.
A shortened summary version of שמונה עשרה

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught
"a shortened form of the eighteen"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that workers daven the full שמונה עשרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different ברייתא lets workers say only a shortened version, so the two sources contradict each other

steps.title: The two sources follow רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the full-שמונה-עשרה ברייתא follows רבן גמליאל, and the shortened-version ברייתא follows רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It is not a contradiction. This ברייתא follows רבן גמליאל, and that ברייתא follows רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת resolves the contradiction by saying each ברייתא follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל holds that a person must always say all eighteen ברכות, so workers say the full תפילה. רבי יהושע allows a shortened version, so workers may shorten it. The two sources simply follow two opinions in an argument.

keyTerms.meaning: תנא who holds that one always says the full שמונה עשרה
תנא who allows a shortened version of שמונה עשרה

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It is not difficult;
this one follows Rabban Gamliel,
phrases.notes: This refers to the argument in the משנה later in this מסכת (ברכות 28b) about the full or shortened שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: that one follows Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא — רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, הָא — רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to follow one opinion and contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: The full-תפילה ברייתא follows רבן גמליאל, and the shortened-תפילה ברייתא follows רבי יהושע

steps.title: Why mention workers if רבי יהושע allows everyone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת: if the shortened-version ברייתא follows רבי יהושע, why does it mention workers specifically, since רבי יהושע lets everyone shorten?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows רבי יהושע, why mention workers in particular? Even any person may shorten it too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב ששת's answer from Step 18 by pointing out a problem with the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע allows every person to say a shortened שמונה עשרה. So if the ברייתא followed him, it would not need to single out workers. The fact that it mentions workers suggests it is teaching a special leniency just for them.
steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is not against the ברייתא itself. It is against רב ששת's claim that the ברייתא follows רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: If it follows Rabbi Yehoshua,
why mention workers specifically?
Even any person may do so too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, מַאי אִירְיָא פּוֹעֲלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's answer in Step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the shortened-תפילה ברייתא follows רבי יהושע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע lets everyone shorten שמונה עשרה, so a ברייתא following him would have no reason to single out workers

steps.title: Both sources follow רבן גמליאל: wage versus meal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. Both ברייתות follow רבן גמליאל. Workers who earn a wage shorten, and workers who work only for a meal say the full שמונה עשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both ברייתות follow רבן גמליאל, and there is no contradiction. One ברייתא is about workers who work for a wage, and the other is about workers who work only for their meal.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the question in step 19, the גמרא gives up on רב ששת's answer and offers a new way to fit the two ברייתות together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the two ברייתות were split between two different תנאים. Now both follow רבן גמליאל, and the difference is how the worker is paid. If he earns a wage, he says the shortened version. If he works only for his meal, he says the full שמונה עשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both sources
And it is not difficult; there is no contradiction
For their meal, meaning food is their only pay

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. The wage-earners are the ones who shorten. The workers paid only with a meal say the full שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: Rather, both this one and that one follow Rabban Gamliel,
and it is not difficult:
here, it is where they work for their wage.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא with the shortened version.

phrases.english: Here, it is where they work for their meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב ששת's answer after the question in step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): wage versus meal, with both ברייתות following one תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות follow different תנאים (רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע)
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבן גמליאל. Wage-earners shorten, and workers paid only with a meal say the full version

steps.title: A ברייתא on how workers shorten ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support. Workers say קריאת שמע and daven. They skip the ברכה before eating bread, and in ברכת המזון they say only two ברכות, joining the third into the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: Workers working for a homeowner say קריאת שמע and daven. When they eat their bread, they do not say a ברכה before it, but afterward they say two ברכות. How? The first ברכה is said in its normal form. In the second, he begins with the ברכה about the land, and they include "בונה ירושלים" inside the ברכה about the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support the wage/meal split. This part lays out the shortened rules, and the next step gives the key condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that workers are allowed to shorten their ברכות to save the employer's time. Here the shortening is in ברכת המזון: two ברכות instead of three, with "בונה ירושלים" folded into the ברכה about the land. Which workers this applies to comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: And indeed it was taught in a ברייתא; here it brings support
The second ברכה of ברכת המזון, thanking for the land
"Who builds Jerusalem", the third ברכה of ברכת המזון

phrases.english: And indeed it was taught:
Workers who were doing work
for a homeowner
recite קריאת שמע and pray.
And they eat their bread
and do not say a ברכה before it,
but they say two ברכות after it.
phrases.notes: "After it" means ברכת המזון, which normally has three main ברכות.

phrases.english: How so?
The first ברכה is said in its normal form,
for the second, he begins with the ברכה of the land
and they include "Who builds Jerusalem" in the ברכה of the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to back up the answer in step 20
steps.raayaObject: That the law for workers depends on whether they are paid a wage or only a meal
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about workers' קריאת שמע, תפילה, and shortened ברכת המזון

steps.title: The shortening applies only to wage-earners
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the shortening applies only to workers who earn a wage. Workers paid only with a meal, or whose employer eats with them, say the ברכות in full.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? To workers who work for a wage. But if they work only for their meal, or if the homeowner eats with them, they say the ברכות in the normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key line of the support. The ברייתא itself makes the same wage-versus-meal split that the גמרא used in step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא limits the shortening to wage-earners. Workers paid only with a meal say the full ברכות. This matches step 20 exactly and shows that this split is a real one taught by a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? It introduces a limit on the rule
Reclines with them, meaning he eats the meal together with them

steps.whatToRemember: Workers who earn a wage may shorten their ברכות and תפילה to save the employer's time. Workers paid only with a meal, or eating with the employer, say everything in full.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
Where they work for their wage,
but if they work for their meal

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּעַל הַבַּיִת מֵיסֵב עִמָּהֶן —
phrases.english: or the homeowner was reclining with them,
they say the ברכות in the normal form.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא started in step 21 and gives the actual point of support
steps.raayaSupportSource: The closing condition of the ברייתא, which makes the same split

steps.title: The משנה: a groom is exempt from קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: a חתן is exempt from קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: A groom is exempt from קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the next rule in the משנה. This sets up the discussion of where the rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new section. The גמרא will now look for the source of the חתן's exemption.

phrases.english: A groom is exempt from the recitation of Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חתן is exempt from קריאת שמע

steps.title: The פסוק source for the exemption
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that one busy with a מצוה is exempt, and specifically that a חתן is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "When you sit in your house" leaves out one who is busy with a מצוה. "And when you walk on the way" leaves out a groom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the source in the פסוק for the משנה's rule about a חתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads two phrases of the פסוק as leaving people out. The first phrase exempts anyone busy with a מצוה. The second exempts a חתן specifically. The ברייתא does not spell out here exactly how the words show this.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught; it introduces a ברייתא
"When you sit in your house", from the first paragraph of שמע
To the exclusion of; leaving out

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"When you sit in your house"
phrases.notes: דברים 6:7

phrases.english: excludes one who is busy with a מצוה.
"And when you walk on the way"
excludes a groom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the משנה just quoted
steps.raayaObject: The חתן's exemption from קריאת שמע
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק בשבתך בביתך ובלכתך בדרך, as read by a ברייתא

steps.title: Groom of a בתולה exempt, groom of an אלמנה obligated
steps.stepSummary: From this reading the ברייתא concludes: one who marries a בתולה is exempt, but one who marries an אלמנה must say קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: one who marries a virgin is exempt, and one who marries a widow is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא draws a practical rule from its reading of the פסוק and limits the groom's exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every groom is exempt. Only a man marrying a בתולה is exempt, and a man marrying an אלמנה must still say קריאת שמע. The ברייתא says this rule comes from the reading it just gave, though it does not explain the reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said; a rule drawn from what came before

steps.whatToRemember: A חתן's exemption from קריאת שמע comes from the פסוק. It applies to one who marries a בתולה, not one who marries an אלמנה.

phrases.english: From here they said:
One who marries a virgin is exempt,
and one who marries a widow is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical limit from the reading of the פסוק in step 24
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only a groom who marries a בתולה is exempt from קריאת שמע. A groom who marries an אלמנה is obligated.

steps.title: How does the verse show this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא's פסוק actually shows that one busy with a מצוה is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is this understood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the words of the פסוק teach that one busy with a מצוה is exempt from קריאת שמע. This question sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 24 learned the exemption for one busy with a מצוה from ״בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ בְּבֵיתֶךָ״, but it is not obvious how. Sitting at home seems to have nothing to do with being busy with a מצוה, so the גמרא wants to see the exact reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Implies, shows. Here it means: how does the verse show this?

phrases.english: What shows this?
phrases.notes: He is asking how ״בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ בְּבֵיתֶךָ״ (דברים 6:7) shows that a person busy with a מצוה is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the ברייתא's derivation from the פסוק works
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the words ״בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ בְּבֵיתֶךָ״ teach that one busy with a מצוה is exempt from קריאת שמע

steps.title: רב פפא: like an optional journey
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the פסוק describes an optional trip, so the obligation applies only during optional activities.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is like the road. Just as a trip on the road is optional, so too here, the obligation applies to optional activities.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. The פסוק talks about walking on the road, which is a normal, optional activity, so קריאת שמע is required only during optional activities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The example the Torah chose, a trip on the road, shows what kind of activity the obligation covers. It is a personal activity that a person chooses to do. Someone busy with a מצוה is not doing something optional, so he is outside the obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains the derivation
Optional, something a person chooses to do and is not a מצוה

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Like the road.
phrases.notes: He means: read 'when you sit in your house' like the trip along the road in the same פסוק.

phrases.english: Just as a road trip is optional,
so too here, it is optional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק's example of a road trip shows that the obligation applies during optional activities, not while doing a מצוה

steps.title: But maybe he is walking to a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: the traveler may be going to do a מצוה, and the Torah still tells him to say קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are we not also dealing with someone who is going to do a מצוה? And even so, the Torah said he should read קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's answer. A person on the road might be traveling to do a מצוה, and the פסוק still obligates him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא assumed every road trip is optional. But the פסוק does not say what the trip is for, so it could include a trip for a מצוה. If so, the פסוק would teach the opposite: even someone busy with a מצוה must say קריאת שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: Are we not dealing with...?, a way of asking whether a case is included
A matter of מצוה, a מצוה errand
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
He should read, meaning say קריאת שמע

phrases.english: Are we not dealing with
someone who is going to do a מצוה,
and even so the Torah said: Let him read.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דְּקָאָזֵיל לִדְבַר מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's reading in step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the road trip in the פסוק is optional
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק does not say what the trip is for, so it may include a trip for a מצוה. That would show that even one busy with a מצוה is obligated.

steps.title: The word "your going" proves the exemption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the Torah wrote ״בְּלֶכְתְּךָ״ (your going) instead of ״בְּלֶכֶת״ (going), which limits the obligation to personal trips.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק say "when going." Why does it say "when you go"? Learn from this: it is your own going that obligates you, but going for a מצוה exempts you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by looking closely at the exact word in the פסוק. The Torah wrote "your going," which teaches that only personal trips obligate you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah meant every trip, it could have just written ״בְּלֶכֶת״, "when going." The added "your" in ״בְּלֶכְתְּךָ״ means going for your own purposes. A trip for a מצוה is not "yours" in this sense, so the person is exempt, and רב פפא's point stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the verse say..., meaning the Torah could have written it differently
When going, the shorter wording the Torah did not use

steps.whatToRemember: ״בְּלֶכְתְּךָ״, your own going, obligates you in קריאת שמע. Going for a מצוה exempts you. This is the source for the rule that one busy with a מצוה, like a חתן, is exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the wider principle that one busy with a מצוה is exempt from another מצוה. It explains why the חתן in the משנה is exempt from קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say "when going."
What is "when you go"?
phrases.notes: The extra ending "you" is what the גמרא is learning from.

phrases.english: Learn from this:
It is in your own going that you are obligated,
but going for a מצוה, you are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 and supports רב פפא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the verse's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק covers every trip, including a trip for a מצוה, so even one busy with a מצוה must say קריאת שמע
steps.terutzMaskana: The word ״בְּלֶכְתְּךָ״ limits the obligation to personal trips, so one going for a מצוה is exempt
